summary: Hosted requests routed to fallback during Dedicated saturation billed at reserved capacity ladder rate
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a subset of their hosted calls were routed to Dedicated fallback capacity during a scheduled Dedicated pool saturation. Those calls were billed using the customer's reserved-capacity ladder rates (hourly reserved price) instead of the hosted fallback price, resulting in a ~42% unexpected increase on today's invoice line items. Impact: billing overcharge for mixed-hosted/dedicated workload during fallback conditions; customer is on a reserved commitment and expects fallback-hosted requests to be billed at hosted-fallback pricing or at least pro-rated correctly.

Observed at: 2026-03-04 23:10 - 2026-03-05 01:15 UTC (customer reported window).

Requested outcome: rapid investigation, provisional credit for the overcharged lines, and a root-cause and mitigation plan to prevent future crossover of pricing ladders in fallback routing paths.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends steady low-latency traffic to hosted endpoint tied to org BlueHarbor Labs. 2) Dedicated pool for their reserved capacity receives a transient saturation event (autoscaler did not add burst GPUs in time). 3) Smart-routing policy falls back to hosted variants for some requests; routing log shows variety of fallback variants. 4) Billing post-processor later attributed those same request IDs to the reserved ladder instead of fallback-hosted pricing.

Notes: reproduction is sensitive to traffic shaping and requires simulating dedicated saturation and routing policy thresholds.

Placing a temporary guard in mapping to prefer final_routed_variant when present.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Billing post-processor keyed pricing ladder off of earliest non-null compute_pool metadata instead of final_routed_variant. This would attribute hosted-fallback traffic to reserved ladder if initial intent was dedicated.
Hypothesis B: Event ordering in the async postback pipeline can cause routing annotations to be processed out-of-order when autoscaler events interleave, leading to stale pool tags being used.
Checked DB: 18 sample request IDs show final_routed_variant='hosted-v2' while billing_request.compute_pool='dedicated-bh-pool-14'.
Temporary mitigation: add explicit rule in billing-mapper to prefer final_routed_variant tag if present. Patch PR linked (runtime PR #4821).
Next steps: run backfill on affected window to recompute pricing at request granularity and generate credit lines; instrument end-to-end trace to verify ordering invariants.
resolution_notes: Provisional credit of $1,280 prepared on 2026-03-07; final credit will be applied after backfill confirms affected invoice lines. Engineering to ship patch to billing-mapper to prefer final_routed_variant and add a unit test to cover async postback ordering. Follow-up: create an alert on mismatch counts between routing logs and billing attribution (INT-1129 created to implement metric).
